content.comment_body: Is it possible to configure a Modbus write so that it only sends the command when the value changes or as specified? I am using a remote Modbus device that has an EEPROM with a write limit of 100000 operations, so writing every cycle or every second will quickly use up its lifespan.
No, that's not feasible. You can only adjust the interval timing in the connection settings.

Check if your Modbus device supports writing to EEPROM only upon receiving a specific command, like an 'enter' instruction used by some equipment. Alternatively, consider making your control system handle the memory update process instead.
Hello, could you specify which sensor you're using (is it manual?), and which register function or unit ID you're aiming to write to?

analysis.insight_summary: A user inquired about triggering Modbus write commands only when data changes to prevent wear on a remote EEPROM-limited device. Responses clarified that such selective writing is not a built-in feature; only fixed intervals are configurable. Advice centered on using workarounds through the Modbus device’s own features or external solutions, rather than relying on [company_name] product capabilities.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes the product can perform Modbus writes conditionally, triggered by data changes, instead of on a strict periodic schedule.
